#6294. Lufthansa Now Requires An Account Just To Check In Online

Buying a ticket and having your booking confirmation will no longer be enough to check in online for many Lufthansa Group flights. The airline group is making a Travel ID account mandatory, adding another requirement to a process that should be simple. A major expansion takes effect today, with departures from the United States following later this month.

According to Lufthansa Group’s notice to travel partners, passengers will increasingly need a Travel ID to check in through the websites and apps of Lufthansa, SWISS, Austrian Airlines, Brussels Airlines, Air Dolomiti, Edelweiss, and Discover Airlines.

The rollout is phased by departure point:

One person can check in multiple travelers using their own Travel ID. Someone assisting another passenger may also use their own account for personal assistance.

Lufthansa presents Travel ID as a convenient way to use one login across its airlines, with stored information and fewer forms to complete. It also promotes personalized offers.

Certainly, a frequent Lufthansa Group passenger would likely find that useful. If you regularly fly Lufthansa, SWISS, and Austrian, having your information available across those airlines can save the annoying hassle of have to re-enter personal details.

A booking reference and surname have long been enough to retrieve a reservation and begin check-in. If additional identity or travel-document checks are necessary, an airline can request those during that process. I don’t understand why creating an account must now be part of obtaining a boarding pass, other than for the collection of data.

I already have more travel accounts than I care to count, but count me in here…I already have a Lufthansa Travel ID and I welcome this. But for an occasional traveler who simply wants to check in for a flight, it creates another step with another password or login process to manage.

Passengers who do not want an account can still check in at the airport. Good, but it does not make the online requirement particularly customer-friendly. Online check-in lets passengers helps passengers save time. Someone traveling with only a carry-on may have no reason to visit a check-in counter at all.

Why make that person choose between opening an account and completing check-in at the airport?

Airlines have spent years encouraging passengers to handle more tasks themselves. That works best when the digital process is easy to use. Adding an enrollment requirement seems like an odd way to improve it.

The exception for tickets issued by other airlines is also worth highlighting….an odd disincentive to book away, it seems to me.

Lufthansa Group is expanding its mandatory Travel ID requirement for online check-in throughout November, including US departures beginning November 16.

I have no objection to a shared account that makes traveling across the group easier. But passengers should be able to decide whether they want one. Buying a ticket ought to be enough to access the basic tools needed to use it like online check-in…

#6293. 9 Best Hotels in Rio de Janeiro for a Taste of the Carioca Lifestyle

“I live where you vacation” takes on a whole other meaning when, like me, you're based in Rio de Janeiro. I live smack in the middle of South America’s two hottest beaches—Copacabana and Ipanema—but it’s not the ocean that keeps me in Brazil's buzziest city. It’s the life that happens around it. It’s the sound of the first coconuts being cut open on the beach in the early morning, the sight of barefoot surfers passing beneath my window, and the honey-like melody of bossa nova flowing from a nearby beach kiosk. Not everyone can live here, of course. But luckily, the best hotels in Rio de Janeiro give you a good taste of what it feels like to be a local in Brazil’s most exciting metropolis.

Over the past six years, I’ve come to appreciate how each neighborhood lets you experience the city differently. Copacabana delivers the high-energy hustle and bustle you’d expect from a place that hosts the biggest Carnival celebration on Earth. In contrast, Leblon offers a quieter, more upscale seaside rhythm. And then there’s Santa Teresa, secluded on the forested hilltops, a tried-and-true bohemian village that’s managed to hold onto its personality despite the city’s rising tourism numbers. The hotels below span these special neighborhoods, with each property offering its own unique take on life in Rio, with Brazilian design, memorable views, and hospitality that’ll make you want to stick around just a little bit longer. Read on for the best hotels in Rio de Janeiro, according to our editors.

For glorious Brazilian beaches, Copacabana is ground zero. But the elegant Copacabana Palace is the hotel that created this place, making this strip of sand famous and helping to conjure the idea of the beach as central to Brazilian identity. When the Copacabana Palace opened over a hundred years ago, it occupied an unheralded neighborhood, amid modest houses and fishermen’s shacks. Until then, Rio de Janeiro had been centered on the old downtown areas of Centro and Castelo, and the 19th-century mansions of leafy Santa Teresa, but a new age of leisure arrived in the post-war years. Sunbathing was suddenly a thing, and Coco Chanel made having a tan fashionable. Designed by French architect Joseph Gire, the Copacabana Palace adopted the elegant Art Deco lines of the grand hotels of the French Riviera. More than a century on, the Copacabana Palace is still a Rio icon, bestriding the Avenida Atlântica on that incomparable bay. The style is classic opulence, with vast chandeliers, acres of marble, and Brazilian hardwoods; a sanctuary among the city’s endless partying. But this is Brazil. The Palace may be grand, but it is also fun. The dining options are fabulous, there is a rooftop tennis court, and, across the avenue on that famous beach, hotel staff attend to guests with umbrellas, loungers, cold towels, and sun lotion. —Stanley Stewart

The modern antidote to the Copacabana Palace’s grand hotel glamour, Philippe Starck’s Brazilian debut—which opened in 2007—has design cred in spades. The 89 all-white rooms have balconies (42 with ocean views), but you’ll want to spend time at the rooftop bar by the infinity pool to gaze at Ipanema, Leblon, the Two Brothers Mountain, and Corcovado; watch the sunset; and sip rum muddled with fresh strawberries, a local fave. Other amenities include a spa, beach service, a fitness center, and bike rentals. Proximity, too, is key: The Fasano is across the street from Ipanema Beach, and a seven-minute walk from General Osório metro and 12 minutes from Copacabana Beach.

The Fairmont Rio de Janeiro Copacabana is a lively beachfront hotel that pairs the comforts of a major luxury brand with the Brazilian energy people come searching for. The 375 rooms and suites are spacious and comfortable, and all come with balconies to enjoy the fabulous views. Speaking of which, the property's signature sixth-floor infinity pool melts into the Copacabana horizon, and everything happens around it: specialty coffee and gelato are served in the roomy lounge, contemporary Brazilian dining is highlighted at the outdoor Marine Restô, and cocktails are enjoyed on loungers and cozy couches around the poolside bar. The pool deck also hosts live music, late-night DJs, and Sunday feijoada (a traditional black bean stew) meals, making this a space where Rio’s visitors and locals collide. Elsewhere, the modern gym has everything you need, and I’d return for the spa alone—the two-hour Fire Ritual treatment is a particular highlight. With ongoing beach activities, weekend yoga, and Ipanema within walking distance, this is a hotel that matches Rio’s upbeat social life.

Think of Hotel Santa Teresa Rio MGallery by Sofitel as a hacienda-style counterpoint to the flashier options on the beach. Part of the mini boutique hotel boom happening in the quiet hilltop neighborhood of Santa Teresa, this former derelict mansion has 44 rooms, all with wood floors and sun-filtering shutters that nod to the tropical surroundings without hitting guests over the head with it. The service can be uneven—veering between over-attentive and indifferent—but the 80-foot pool, with its view over Santa Teresa’s stately villas and the glittering waters of Guanabara Bay, and lush gardens more than make up for it. The spa here is worth checking out, too.

Subtle and modern, in contrast to the go-go party scene of the Fasano, Emiliano was a welcome addition to Rio’s oceanfront Avenida Atlântica when it opened in 2016. A five-star SLH property, the 90 rooms and suites—spread across 12 floors—are large and filled with lovely touches like plants and plump white sofas that make it feel like your own sophisticated beachside apartment, while the bathrooms have huge showers and bathtubs. Plus, beach access is great: It's right across the street from the southern part of Copacabana Beach. Be sure to enjoy the rooftop infinity pool overlooking the ocean.

With 51 rooms, Janeiro has the intimacy of a boutique hotel with the five-star service of a much larger luxury brand. Sitting across the street from Leblon Beach, one of the city’s most beautiful stretches of ocean, the beachy property's interior design reflects the effortlessly chic aesthetic of co-owner Oskar Metsavaht, founder of Brazilian fashion label Osklen. Monochromatic tones, warm wood, and oversized windows keep Rio’s natural surroundings front and center in all rooms. Thoughtful touches like yoga mats, afternoon tea service, exceptionally plush robes, and complimentary Ipanema flip-flops make the stay feel more personal than most. The breakfast service feels like being secretly let into a bakery, with warm pão de queijo (Brazilian cheese bread) promptly delivered directly to your table, and a colorful assortment of bread spread out over the bar. Downstairs, Cedilha draws a cool crowd for New York–style bistro dinners, while the rooftop plunge pool frames the twin-peaked Two Brothers Mountain through a circular window. Beach service, bicycles, and nearby gym access make settling into Rio’s laid-back lifestyle easy.

Form meets function at Ipanema Inn, an independently owned urban hotel just one block from the world-famous Ipanema Beach. This thoughtfully designed property channels Brazilian modernism through midcentury furniture by designer Sergio Rodrigues, natural materials, and rooms that range from compact courtyard-facing doubles to a duplex suite with sweeping mountain vistas and space for the whole family. At ground level, Quitéria, the acclaimed in-house restaurant, spills out onto the mosaic sidewalk of Rua Maria Quitéria, where chef David Cruz serves a refined menu sourced from small Brazilian producers. Breakfast runs until 11:30 a.m., staff is among the warmest you'll encounter anywhere, and complimentary bikes connect you to a segregated coastal path stretching from Leme all the way to Leblon. With the metro two minutes away and three of Brazil's hottest designer boutiques within the same radius, this is Rio at its most stylish and convenient. —Patrick Gray

An effortless oceanside social hub with modernist Brazilian design notes, Hotel Arpoador is known for its cool, carefree style and on-site wellness offerings. I first visited Hotel Arpoador when it reopened in 2019 and noticed its unique setting: Arpoador is on one of the only stretches of coastline in Rio that is traffic-free. Returning several years later, I rediscovered a hotel that has become a modern classic on the Rio scene, and the freshness is a joy to behold. Do as I do and head down to spend your days surrounded by the spectacle of Rio’s famous beach culture. Hotel Arpoador offers a beach service with chairs, umbrellas, towels, and staff that can look after your belongings as you frolic in the frothy, wild Atlantic. Be sure to make time to enjoy the rooftop with its triangular pool and panoramic ocean views, as well as the Maré Spa wellness space with its excellent treatments and steam room. And don't forget to grab a drink at Arp Bar—with its in-the-know crowd that spills out onto the beachfront from dawn to dusk, it has become the beating heart of Rio’s social scene. —P.G.

Set on a hilltop in the historic Santa Teresa neighborhood, Chez Georges is a striking example of Brazilian Brutalism, offering sweeping 360-degree views of Sugarloaf Mountain and Guanabara Bay. Just a 20-minute drive from the vibrant Copacabana Beach, its secluded setting feels like an urban retreat, where time slows down and the morning begins with the gentle sound of birds. Whether lounging by the 50-foot pool, listening to soft Brazilian music from the record player, or watching the sunset, Chez Georges offers a tranquil, almost dreamlike escape. While Chez Georges may be modest in size, with only a handful of suites, the rooms themselves feel anything but small. Each suite is designed with ’70s-inspired minimalism. Inside, you'll find a standard wardrobe, desk, and king-size bed, but it’s the floor-to-ceiling windows that steal the show, opening onto a shared balcony with sweeping views that are perfect for watching the sunrise. —Kayla Brock

What is the best neighborhood in Rio de Janeiro to stay in?

For a first visit, I’d choose Ipanema. You have the beach, excellent restaurants, Brazilian boutiques, and metro stations all within easy reach—and it’s very much a lived-in neighborhood, teeming with locals and businesses around the clock.

What is the nicest hotel in Rio de Janeiro?

For classic luxury, Copacabana Palace gets my vote. The century-long history, grand beachfront setting, celebrated pool, and attentive service make staying here feel like you’re playing a part in Rio's story.

How we choose the best hotels in Rio de Janeiro

Every hotel review on this list has been written by a Condé Nast Traveler journalist who knows the destination and has visited that property. When choosing hotels, our editors consider properties across price points that offer an authentic and insider experience of a destination, keeping design, location, service, and sustainability credentials top of mind.

#6292. A Flight Only Bookable With Points Offers Amazing Winter Sun

I often tell people that the best unkept secret with Avios is, in fact, the Avios app. Separate to the British Airways app, the Avios app allows users to set flight alerts and goals, but also gives a heads up about opportunities before they appear anywhere else.

Case in point: before a press release had even hit my inbox, the Avios app alerted me that an ‘Avios only’ flight had just launched. This isn’t the first time Avios has launched a flight only bookable with points, but it is the first time they’ve done one to CAPE TOWN, during peak winter break time.

British Airways and Avios have collaborated on a flight only bookable with Avios, where every seat on the plane is available for sale with points. First, business, premium and economy, all available using Avios. The flights depart as follows…

As noted, these flights are now bookable and if history repeats itself, they won’t be available for long. This plane only has 8 seats in first, so get in quick! One amazing thing about Avios is that they aren’t just the currency of one airline, but a whopping seven. If you have any points with Finnair, Iberia, Qatar, Aer Lingus, Logainair, Vueling or British Airways you can pool points together to book these flights.

Avios is also a transfer partner of Amex, Bilt, Capital One, Chase and plenty of other global financial institutions, so there should be ample opportunity to convert bank points into Avios and get these booked. Hot tip though, ensure there are seats available before you make your transfer, since this will be a hot commodity.

I love any airline rewarding members with flights entirely bookable with points. What makes this one different is that it’s not some off peak, off season destination. It’s Cape Town, easily one of the toughest tickets with any currency, during peak time, perfect for people looking to ditch the weather for the holidays and catch NYE in one of the best cities on earth.

Yes, Cape Town is by far one of my favorites and for any oenophiles, a trip to nearby Stellenbosch or Franschoek is a must. Standard luggage limits apply, so definitely bring enough suitcases to haul back wine. Fin. Head to British Airways website to book.

The IHG Milestone Rewards program offers useful benefits, including IHG One Rewards points or food-and-beverage rewards at most tiers, and confirmable suite upgrades at some tiers. Plus, you can choose an IHG annual lounge membership at the 40- and 70-night tiers.

Most IHG hotels and resorts don't offer club lounges, but if you want to access the club lounge at IHG properties that do have one, you'll need to do one of the following:

Also, keep in mind that even if an IHG property upgrades you to a club-level room, you won't automatically get access to the lounge. At IHG club lounges, you typically get complimentary breakfast and nonalcoholic drinks throughout the day. You will sometimes even get afternoon tea, evening drinks and hors d'oeuvres.

Here's everything you need to know about IHG's annual lounge membership, including how to earn and use it.

IHG's annual lounge membership — which you can earn through IHG's Milestone Rewards program — provides lounge access for one member and a guest if you stay at an IHG property with a club lounge.

An annual lounge membership gets you access to the club lounge and its amenities during your stay. However, IHG's terms and conditions allow for lounge access to be restricted "due to renovations, closures, or other facility limitations." This membership also doesn't include Club Regent or Club InterContinental amenities or services beyond the physical lounge.

According to IHG's terms and conditions, an annual lounge membership provides access to club lounges on qualified stays, including reward nights and free nights. During stays at participating Iberostar Beachfront Resorts, an annual lounge membership gives you access to the Star Prestige facilities and services (but not to Star Prestige rooms). However, an annual lounge membership doesn't include access to the lounges at InterContinental Alliance Resorts in Macao.

Unfortunately, there's no quick way to determine which IHG hotels in a particular city have club lounges. Instead, I've found it most efficient to simply check whether a specific hotel displays rooms with lounge access in the room's name or description.

Related: The 19 best IHG hotels in the world

The only way to earn an IHG annual lounge membership is to select it as a 40- or 70-night Milestone Reward. You'll earn IHG Milestone Rewards as you reach the following tiers each calendar year:

Once you reach a milestone, you'll have 90 days to select your Milestone Reward. If you don't make a selection within that period, you'll forfeit the reward.

Once you select an annual lounge membership as a Milestone Reward, it will be valid through the end of the calendar year following the year in which you earned the Milestone Reward. So, if you reached the 40- or 70-night milestone during this year and selected an annual lounge membership, the pass will be valid through Dec. 31 of next year.

Related: How much value does the IHG One Rewards program provide when you book directly?

Between earning an IHG annual lounge membership and its expiration, there's no limit to the number of times you can use your membership.

When you check into an IHG hotel or resort with a club lounge, show the front desk staff your annual lounge membership. You can find your memberships in your IHG account's "Rewards Wallet" under "Rewards to enhance your stay." Click "Redeem," and show the resulting page to the front desk staff. The staff will then add club lounge access to your room key or tell you how to access the lounge.

You can only use your annual lounge membership if you are the primary member of a qualifying stay. An IHG spokesperson told TPG that the member with the annual lounge membership must be the primary member on the reservation so "the hotel will be able to confirm the existence of the Annual Lounge Pass in the account."

In addition to brands like InterContinental, where you might expect to find a club lounge, you'll occasionally find that other IHG brands (like Crowne Plaza and Holiday Inn) offer lounges.

Related: The best IHG all-inclusive resorts for every type of traveler

So, should you select an annual lounge membership at the 40- or 70-night milestone? And should you strive to stay 40 nights at IHG hotels to earn an annual lounge membership as one of your Milestone Rewards choices?

Unfortunately, the answer isn't always a clear "yes" or "no." My husband has maintained an annual lounge membership since early 2023, so I've visited several IHG lounges during the last three years. All the club lounges I've visited offered a good selection of food and drinks, including complimentary alcoholic drinks in the evenings. So, I've been satisfied with our decision to select an annual lounge membership at the 40-night Milestone Rewards tier each year.

However, you'll also want to consider how much you think you'll use an IHG annual lounge membership. Specifically, you may want to consider how important club lounge availability is to you in the destinations you'll visit. For example, we chose the InterContinental Cartagena de Indias in Colombia and the Holiday Inn Singapore Atrium primarily because their award rates were reasonable and we knew the properties had club lounges.

Once you decide the value you think an annual lounge membership would provide, consider the value you'd get from the other Milestone Rewards choices at the 40- or 70-night tier. For example, at the 40-night milestone tier, would you value having 10,000 bonus points, five $20 food-and-beverage rewards or one confirmable suite upgrade more than an annual lounge membership? TPG's October 2026 valuations peg the 10,000 bonus points at about $60, while five $20 food-and-beverage rewards will be worth around $100.

Related: Which credit card should you use for IHG stays?

I've been happy with IHG's annual lounge membership. If you stay at several IHG hotels with club lounges each year, I expect you'll also find it worth selecting an annual lounge membership through IHG's Milestone Rewards program after staying 40 or 70 nights each calendar year.

However, if you rarely stay at IHG hotels and resorts with club lounges, frequently travel with more than one other person or don't value lounge access, you might not get enough value from an annual lounge membership to justify selecting it over other Milestone Rewards at the 40- or 70-night tiers.

#6290. Your November 2026 Horoscope: We're Turning a Corner This Month—and Your Travels Are Too

Steph Koyfman is a writer and astrologer best known for her work as Lady Cazimi. She writes the monthly horoscope for Condé Nast Traveler's Women Who Travel.

Your November 2026 horoscope is here—and it comes bearing some good news. After last month’s emotional whiplash, it will feel like a relief to experience the course-correction that November’s astrology has in store for us. Mercury and Venus both station direct on November 13, bringing us greater clarity by mid-month.

Venus began her retrograde deep dive in early October, provoked by a sense that something was deeply wrong. Mercury followed suit later that month, aiding Venus’ soul-searching with its thorough detective work. Many of us may have revisited our prior trauma as new revelations dawned on us, or maybe as newfound revulsion made itself felt at the way we’d been mistreated. Still more of us probably spent the last few weeks changing our minds and hearts about someone or something important to us. It’s not sustainable to love something that doesn’t love you back, and perhaps there’s a deep lack of equity in these dynamics that was crying out for repair. Now, the period of reappraisal is concluding, but this is not a return to “normalcy” so much as it is a return to “a way of relating that we can live with because it’s true.”

Venus also ends its retrograde in much better shape than it started. All month, Venus will be in its home sign of Libra forming a supportive sextile to Jupiter. Something is being restored to us this month, and something is being brought back into balance. Whether it’s harmony, equity, justice, or just an ability to get along with (or without) someone you had deep misgivings about in October, we will probably leave this month feeling better about where we’ve left things. Possibly, we will also be celebrating positive wins and turning points in our lives. This is one of the better moments of 2026 for the lovers, romantics, and adventurers, especially once the Sun enters Sagittarius on November 22 and makes us restless to explore new horizons again. If you’ve got travel planned this month, you will find plenty of beauty to appreciate, even if you’re not in the most stereotypically postcard-perfect location.

Astrologer's note: Below we refer to your signs as “rising” signs, also known as your ascendant sign. Horoscopes are more accurate when read this way—using your birth time and location, you can quickly find your rising sign online (it takes less than 30 seconds).

Things are looking up for one or more of your significant relationships. It was hard-won progress alright, but Venus is stationing direct in your 7th house of partnerships this month, and she’s in strong shape after the trials of October. Hopefully, all that soul-searching and probing and re-opening of the can of worms from years ago did what it needed to do, and by the looks of it, couple’s therapy was probably a sound investment. It’s only by addressing things at the root that you can come back together again in a way that feels real. And if dredging up all that sordid material made it impossible to go home again, there is also a version of this story where you’re now coming back into alignment with yourself after grieving the end of a friendship or relationship. If anything, you’re more clear than ever before on what you want for your relationships going forward, and you’ve prepped the soil to cultivate better unions in the future. You are the consummate “girl who’s gonna be okay.”

In general, this would be a cute time to take a honeymoon with your boo or bestie — really anyone important in your life who has been a meaningful part of your journey as of late. November’s astrology is stimulating the parts of your chart that are most associated with romance, fun, and adventure, and even if you’re fearless when it comes to traveling solo, you’ll probably want someone by your side to share this one with. After the Sun enters Sagittarius on November 22, you’ll be even more in the zone to go places and glimpse new horizons, so enjoy the mood while it lasts.

This month could also represent an important turning point in one of your financial endeavors—the kind that typically looks like you signing on the dotted line. If last month’s storms threw a contract, agreement, or joint venture into question, things should hopefully clear up enough by mid-month for you to feel confident about moving forward with the updated version. Mercury will station direct in your 8th house of shared resources on the same day as Venus (November 13), and there’s a new moon in Scorpio on November 9 that signals some sort of new beginning in this area. However, this might require you to “kill your darlings” to get there. You might be really attached to the version of your masterpiece you originally envisioned in your mind’s eye, but November’s Mars-Jupiter-South Node conjunction has other plans in mind for you. Don’t let your pride get in the way of what could be a much better deal for everyone involved. This is an inevitable part of any creative process.

The vibes were pretty off there for a second, but the good news is that you’re coming back to yourself now (and potentially even setting yourself up to feel better than ever). With your ruling planet, Venus, stationing direct with shining colors on November 13, it seems as though the winter of your discontent is now transforming into a proverbial spring of renewal. The most likely culprit? Something is realigning in your life to restore your health and wellbeing. Whether you’re implementing a healing protocol, lifestyle adjustment, or even getting more help around the house or at your job, it will feel as though a burden is being lifted. Some of you might even be adopting a new pet who will get you out the door every day on walks or otherwise rebalance the harmony in your home for the better. Celebrate the wins wherever you can, because you certainly went through enough to deserve them.

Though you will probably enjoy a greater sense of wellbeing in November (even to the point of whistling while you work), this is bigger than just what’s happening right now. Whatever ordeal you went through these last few weeks is ultimately setting you up for a new eight-year chapter in your relationships, work, and relationship to your body. New ways of relating will emerge from this moment, as well as different types of projects you will feel called to pursue. Perhaps there will be new collaborators and colleagues entering your life over the next few months—a definitive turning of the page in your work. Pay attention to the clarity that’s emerging right now in your conversations with other people (especially on November 4, 9, and 13), because some of the things that muddied the waters recently are getting sorted by mid-month—if not in a totally pleasant way, then at least in a clear way. You want to feel known and seen by the people you’re devoted to, and that has to begin with a clear foundation of honesty and trust.

This month’s astrology lends itself more to a healing retreat than a party weekend or a heavy-duty sightseeing adventure, but if life hasn’t handed you the luxury of a quiet vacation, you will still be inclined to prioritize the things that make you feel best—a short gym workout at the hotel before you start your day, not skipping your morning meditation just because you’re not at home, making sure you eat a substantial breakfast with protein before you’re off to the races, you get the vibe. If you’re gonna turn a new leaf, make sure you’re not doing so from the place of self-neglect you just worked so hard to come back from.

It feels like you’re approaching some sort of cliffhanger or climax in your story, and this is not going to be one of the more predictable outcomes you’ve experienced. As your ruling planet, Mercury, stations direct on November 13 to deliver its investigative report from the last couple of weeks, the full moon in Gemini on November 24 brings you a bit of a twist or surprise ending to the bigger journey you’ve been on this year. This full moon is conjunct Uranus, so its effect on your life will likely be destabilizing and disruptive, even if not entirely unexpected. Then again, maybe the surprise is that you’ve actually got more options than you thought. A change will be made, that’s for sure. But maybe you have some real agency to work with.

With Mercury concluding its retrograde in your 6th house, it’s very possible that you’ll be getting some news related to your health or a diagnosis you sought a second opinion about. There could also be turnover happening at work (like layoffs and reorganizations) that will affect your day-to-day responsibilities going forward. Not to be overlooked is Venus going direct on the same day as Mercury, which very much looks like reaching internal clarity related to matters of the heart. Yes, this could be about your love life, and it could be about your kids (or your decision to have them), but it’s also about the things you love broadly—the pursuits and activities that you would rather organize your life around. You may not see the full trajectory yet, but this could be a real turning point for your creative direction if there’s a labor of love that wants to come through you. But first, there’s the practical matter of finding the hours in a day to bring it forth.

If you feel your heart opening to life again in a real way, that’s par for the course. While the more pivotal changes are rearranging your life, take November as an opportunity to embrace what brings you joy. Make your social life a bigger priority. Spend quality time with your kids. Start going on dates again. Take a trip to one of your favorite places, or better yet, convince yourself that you actually do need to go on an artist’s retreat, and that it can’t wait until next year. You’re in a more fertile, creative headspace than usual, and it would be a shame to let that go to waste.

Home is where the heart is, and maybe that’s never felt more true to you than it does right now. As Venus and Mercury both conclude their retrograde journeys on November 13, you will look around you and perhaps realize that everything you need is right here, exactly where you are. And if you’re not there yet, then you’re probably well on your way, because these last few weeks have ultimately been a rehoming process for you. Barring a literal move, there have been old emotions coming up to be dealt with connected to places where you once lived, as well as more recent issues that have likely changed the dynamics within your family. You’ve had children to consider, as well as questions of how to continue your legacy in general. You’ve been deep in your feels about a lover too, as though you didn’t already have enough on your mind, and maybe opening your heart to love again is part of the bigger life change you’re considering. Where is your root system anchored, and who does it connect you to? This is ultimately the question that steers you forward.

For some of you, these shifts could be quite literal. Venus spends all of November forming a sextile to Jupiter, which offers you some monetary assistance to put toward your home (or at least opens a way financially to make things happen). Whether you’re buying a house, starting a new lease, or investing in some home improvement, there’s likely enough to keep you occupied at home right now that travel is not top of mind (or in your budget). If you do go anywhere this month, it will likely be a visit to see family or scout a place you're considering a move to. Themes of “homecoming” are loud for you right now, and besides, many of us need to plan our visits home around the difficult astrology. November is probably one of the better times for you to spend among the people you’ve known the longest.

Things are also moving forward for you when it comes to your creative projects and hobbies (and look, if you needed a green light to get back on the dating apps, it’s probably safe to come out from hiding too). The new moon in Scorpio on November 9, followed by Mercury’s direct station in the same sign on November 13, signals new beginnings and forward motion related to the things that bring you a sense of personal fulfillment. If you’ve recently returned to an old favorite pastime, resurrected an old artistic medium that’s been lying dormant, or started patronizing your favorite live music establishments again, that’s a sign to keep going. Follow that thread to its logical conclusion, which is back to the pulse of what makes you feel most alive.

It feels like nothing can stand in your way right now—nothing, that is, but your own unchecked pride. Mid-month, an interesting and rare triple conjunction of Mars, Jupiter, and the South Node constellates in Leo, pumping you up with confidence and motivation to go all the way for the gold. And you might succeed in winning! For now, at least. This is the sort of signature that could hand you a false or empty victory, or perhaps steal your thunder in some way despite whatever you’ve achieved. It could be that you win the battle but not the larger war, or get something you thought you wanted only to find that the spoils don’t taste as sweet as you imagined. This is probably not the time to get carried away with whatever adrenaline high you’re on, or to let yourself get prematurely cocky. Humility and grace (whether it’s in victory or defeat) will be your best allies this month.

This conjunction goes exact on November 15 and 16, though it’ll be in effect all month. Then, between the 17th and the 19th, your ruling planet, the Sun, will form a square to this configuration. It will probably feel as though you’re turning a corner past the point of no return, redeeming yourself as hometown hero only to learn very quickly that you can’t go home again. With Venus and Mercury also stationing direct mid-month, certain chapters are reaching a natural end for you right now when it comes to home, family, and the familiar faces that have surrounded you for so long. Yes, this is probably about where you live physically, but more than that even, it’s about friendships and community. A large amount of our friendships are situational, meaning they’re formed and maintained so long as we’re in the same environment. Also, it’s normal for something like half of your social circle to experience turnover every seven years due to changes in people’s life circumstances. You’re in one of those apex turnover moments right now, and that’s a bittersweet thing to accept. Hopefully Venus’ presence in Libra this month paves the way for some cute hangouts, reunions, and weekend trips.

Things improve for you considerably at the end of the month once the Sun enters Sagittarius on the 22nd and Mars leaves Leo on the 25th. Think: less drama, more levity and fun, and not feeling so much immediate pressure to rise to the occasion and perform. Maybe you can enjoy some nights out again now that you’re no longer training for the Olympics? Late November through early December would be a decent time for you to take a vacation or staycation, or just to generally get back to living life to the fullest. Your joy can’t be deferred indefinitely. Right now, you’ve got permission to let it take center stage.

Guess what! You can probably stop obsessing over whatever you’ve been working on and trust that it’s ready to see the light of day. Mercury and Venus both station direct on November 13, bringing a period of deep revision to a close and priming you for a new chapter in your finances or in the marketplace. Then, the full moon in Gemini on November 24 shines a light on your career and accomplishments, signaling a milestone that you’ve been building up to all year. For you, this is a month that feels like reaching a finish line, though perhaps one that comes with a surprise twist or ending. Either this won’t go entirely as planned, or you’re about to surprise the world by rebranding yourself in an unexpected way. It’s kinda chic to subvert people’s expectations and refuse to be easily siloed or categorized.

Assuming you’re not hard-launching a new offer, redesign, or new position entirely, there are still subtle ways that you’re shifting into a new gear right now. So much of this boils down to how you sell what you’ve got to offer, which is ultimately a reflection of how you see yourself. It’s also about what you choose to prioritize and assign value to. You might say that you don’t care about keeping up appearances, but your credit card statement suggests otherwise. At the very least, you’ll have more actionable data at your fingertips to help you see where you’re misaligned.

You also stand to have some interesting experiences on the road in November. As your ruling planet, Mercury, stations direct in your 3rd house, feelings of deja vu abound, or maybe just coming full circle after getting sidetracked on the scenic route. This is the sort of setup that could send you on a literal road trip to see someone from your past, or to return to a place you didn’t think you’d visit more than once. November 4 is one of the more significant and revealing days for you this month. What’s lost becomes found, what was misunderstood becomes clear, and what needed to go wrong to get you on this path to begin with starts to make a little more sense. This would be the day to have a clarity talk, to have one last stab at editing a draft that hasn’t been coming together, or to go on a sightseeing adventure you know will blow your mind.

Whatever you do, don’t bite off more than you can chew just because your productivity is flowing again. Mars will enter Virgo on November 25, and it’s getting ready to go retrograde in January. This is your early heads up to avoid taking on extra last-minute work at the end of the year. The rest of the world is slowly entering “circle back after the holidays” mode, and you should too.

You’re in full phoenix mode this month, and your glow-up will probably be studied by future generations. Okay, maybe if we’re keeping our expectations realistic, you might splurge on one new skincare product this month that will have a ripple effect on your gorgeousness for years to come. When Venus stations direct in Libra on November 13, you won’t immediately see the complete impact of the inner alchemy you’ve undergone over the last few weeks, but you will feel a shift for the better, and you might even reach some sort of significant personal milestone.

The point is that you’re entering a new eight-year era of your life and more formally leaving behind the one that started at the end of 2018. You can safely start to discard the identity you’ve been wearing that belongs to a bygone version of yourself, and you’re encouraged to adopt a new look or style to assist your becoming. Yes, it will be “safe” to pursue the haircut, makeover, or beauty treatment you’ve been mulling over after mid-November, so this would be the time to travel somewhere for glam purposes. And travel you very well may, because the November 24 full moon in Gemini might find you in the midst of a peak jetsetting experience somewhere you’ve been wanting to go for a while, or perhaps wrapping up an educational or spiritual journey of some sort. You might even end up there unexpectedly, so if you’re reading this at the beginning of November and thinking you don’t have anything planned, make room for a spontaneous plot twist.

Whatever you’re doing, it will be with the abundant support and applause of your friends, community, and wider audience. Venus spends all month in a supportive sextile with Jupiter, which multiplies your blessings through the sheer force of your support network. Don’t be shy about inviting your entire email list to your launch party or opening night, because your victory will feel that much sweeter with other people there to celebrate you. This might be the month to announce something publicly on your socials, and to ask your community to signal boost you.

Last but not least, pay attention to what’s shifting in your finances this month. There are likely delayed answers and payments making their way to you now, as well as a deeper sense that you’re accessing new levels in your earning potential. This new era of yours will likely involve changes to your income, style, personal branding, and new ways of investing in yourself more generally. It’s a good time to get your ducks in a row, scan your accounting for errors and redundancies, and maybe even come up with a new budget.

You’re coming to terms with where you’re at, but that also implies that it’s inherently not where you hoped you’d be by now. Even your recent victories could feel hollow for whatever reason, like you’ve won the trophy you were competing for but it didn’t actually feel as good as you imagined it would. Are you being overly hard on yourself? Probably! But there’s also something to gain from your current sense of dis-ease—namely, spiritual knowledge of who you’re becoming, because you’re no longer easily impressed by the things a previous version of yourself thought would signal that you’ve “made it.”

On one hand, we’re finishing up a Venus Retrograde this month that sent you to hell in October, or maybe at best, had you not feeling so hot. Mercury also stations direct in Scorpio on the same day as Venus (November 13). Your soul-searching is concluding mid-month, backed up by plenty of receipts and evidence of what really transpired. Whether you’re navigating heartbreak on account of someone else or merely self-loathing on account of yourself, you have the spiritual momentum at your disposal to change what you don’t like about yourself and bury your bitterness so that you’re no longer poisoning yourself with the resentment that should be someone else’s cross to bear. You have the conditions at your fingertips to rewrite the narrative you have about yourself. You are moving into a definitive new personal era, and it will be fertilized, but not defined by, your own past disappointments.

Some juicy insight arrives on November 4, when Mercury conjoins the Sun in Scorpio. The new moon in Scorpio on November 9 whispers directions to you about the new path you’re embarking on. But the most potent threshold you’ll be crossing will be roughly between November 13 and 17, which is really the moment where you decide to cut your losses and move on. This is powerful stuff, and it will probably feel equal parts bad and freeing. What would feel like a relief to let go off at this point in your story?

You will probably be too preoccupied with heavy-hitting life things this month to fully escape on vacation, even if you’re fortunate enough to get one. That said, this is definitely a setup for one of those life-altering trips where you “really find yourself,” or at least find the internal clarity and courage to make a change you’ve been putting off. Let the road remind you of who you really are.

This month, you get to gradually free yourself from a jail of uncertainty. Yes, it was warranted to wait for all the facts to come in, and yes, you needed to go deep into your own subjective knowing, which meant quieting the voices from the peanut gallery for a while. To be totally fair, you probably still need more downtime, and you’re invited to remain in seclusion mode until the Sun enters Sagittarius on November 22, which is when you might feel your actual life force returning to you. Until then, don’t feel bad if you prefer to hang back, stay in, and go on a solo journey without your usual companions. You will return to your social engagements in due time, and with much more internal clarity around those connections to boot.

On November 13, Mercury and Venus both station direct in tandem, giving you the clarity and closure to make up your mind about some friendships and acquaintances you were feeling unsure about. You may have very well decided to step away from a group or social scene over these last few weeks, and perhaps that really threw a wrench in a team project or collective effort you’ve been a part of. Harmony and consensus is possible again in November, but that could look different depending on whether you’ve decided to stay or go. The bigger picture is that you’re now in a better position to recognize who your real friends and allies are, which will probably initiate you into a new era of belonging that will affect your social life for years going forward. Knowing who your people are is one thing—finding a club that would have someone like you as a member is another. The rooms you enter between now and March could significantly alter your life trajectory.

It’s no accident that this finds you at a moment when you’re letting go of what you thought you knew about the world. Your ruling planet, Jupiter, will be forming a triple conjunction with Mars and the South Node in your 9th house all month (though this aspect is most exact between November 12 and 16). The last thing you want to do at a time like this is be overly dogmatic or arrogant. You can fight the good fight from a mantle of humility, because stepping into this next phase of your life will probably require you to admit that you were wrong about certain things. You stand to have some interesting learning experiences this month, and those could very well find you on the road. You might find yourself immersed in another culture’s religion, politics, or creation myths, even if all you had in mind was relaxing on the beach with a beer in your hand. If you get the opportunity to go somewhere unfamiliar to you, be less of an evangelist and more of a disciple. The world opens up to you when you stop needing to be so sure about it.

It looks like you’re finally getting your flowers this month, however long overdue they may be. There are likely things that are popping off for you careerwise in November, as well as favorable recognition directed your way more broadly for all the good you do for the world around you. Venus and Mercury both station direct in tandem on November 13, and in the most public-facing parts of your chart to boot. This is partially about how the rest of the world views you and your considerable impact, yes. But this could also feel like a concrete turning point for you that reorients you to accept the next stage of your life’s mission. Venus retrogrades in the same part of the sky every 8 years, so you could handily think of this as an initiation into your next major era. Perhaps this one will have more investor money behind it? Venus remains in a supportive sextile to Jupiter all month, which lends you tangible and immaterial support to make your dreams feasible.

With the full moon in Gemini following close behind Mercury’s direct station on November 24, you might also be wrapping up a project or team effort that’s preoccupied you for much of the year. There were probably setbacks and problems to troubleshoot, but those issues look like they’ll be resolved by the end of the month, and you will finally get to move on to the work you’re most excited about doing. Spoiler: the problem was likely not what you suspected. The results of the audit or root cause assessment may surprise you.

With that busier season of your life concluding (for now), you will probably have a chance to catch your breath at the end of the month. After the Sun enters Sagittarius on November 22, you enter your annual month of solitude and downtime, which typically makes you more inclined to turn down social invitations as the rest of the world is also preparing to hibernate for the holidays. Mars enters Virgo on November 25, though, which energizes your capacity to go places and take on the world. Maybe this year’s rest season calls for a more active style of decompression, preferably not at home in your sweatpants? Mars won’t guarantee you a smooth journey (in fact, it may problematize it, or make you prone to encountering more people with a bad attitude abroad), but it might give you the energy to tackle an itinerary you didn’t have the bandwidth to handle earlier in the year.

Not that you really doubted or underestimated yourself before, but you’re coming out of this month feeling clearer than ever on who you are and what you stand for. All of the projections in the world couldn’t derail you from your mission, and even this most recent trial will ultimately serve as fertile compost for the next major chapter of your career or personal becoming. With Venus and Mercury both stationing direct on November 13, you will feel ready by mid-month to go live with your redesigned website, so to speak. Venus has taken you on a bit of an underworld journey since early October to get in touch with where your purpose is leading you next in life, and Mercury’s shorter retrograde since late October has involved some more technical or logistical revisions to your public-facing materials. It’s not just about the “what” of what you’re doing, but also the “why.”

Don’t assume that this is strictly limited to your professional endeavors, either. Venus’ retrograde journey may have very well brought you face-to-face with matters concerning your family of origin or nationality. You might be entering a new chapter where your relationship to your parents is concerned, and perhaps renewing your ties to your heritage in some way. With Venus stationing direct in your 9th house all month, a long journey to reunite you with loved ones (or with something more intangible) is very probable, and you will probably enjoy connecting with others one-on-one wherever you go. This is probably one of your best moments in 2026 to travel in general, and to take pleasure in your learning pursuits. Make sure to leave time for all the museums, live music, and ambiance-forward restaurants your heart craves. The vibes will be immaculate.

Aside from all of that, there does seem to be a relationship story happening for you this month, and perhaps it’s the kind you’ll welcome. The full moon in Gemini on November 24 could show up for you as a peak romantic experience of some kind, and Venus’ direct station could pave the way for some sort of travel affair, or a relationship with someone from a different culture. However, there’s also a triple conjunction of Mars, Jupiter, and the South Node in your 7th house of others happening all through November, which suggests you’ll need to let go of a need for certainty or a desire to “conquer” or win anyone over prematurely. If you’re coupled, perhaps you and your partner will need to work through some issues and let go of a need to be right or to “win” the argument? Love should be a team effort, not a competition that produces winners and losers. Sacrifice this tendency, and you’ll open yourself up to much more love and satisfaction.

As much as you wish you could focus on more exciting things, you can’t put off dealing with your health concerns any longer. Assuming there are any illnesses and injuries vying for your attention, you will probably be focused on healing and getting to the root of these issues in November. Your ruling planet, Jupiter, conjoins the South Node in your 6th house on November 12, and Mars will join the pile on the 15th and 16th. This is certainly a recipe for overdoing it at the gym, so don’t push yourself too hard if you’ve got the extra fuel to burn. Other than that, what does the doctor say? Does it make sense to get a second opinion? Do you need to make a lifestyle adjustment? This is not the sexy horoscope you were hoping for, but it’s quite possibly the one you need right now.

Fortunately, with Venus stationing direct in Libra all month and forming a sextile to Jupiter, you will probably find ways to access the resources you need to make a proper recovery. Be it money, insurance payouts, or any other kind of help from friends and family you might need while you’re on bedrest or whatever else, there is something beautiful happening with this embrace of interdependency in your life. Maybe you started this Venus Retrograde in October feeling cynical that people would really be there for you, or that a safety net would appear when you needed it. The most important shifts currently happening in your life are the ones that correct the balance of reciprocity and make you feel supported.

And if your health is fine? More than likely, it’s your job that isn’t. Budget cuts, layoffs, and bureaucratic red tape could all conspire to make your life more difficult. However, it still seems as though a solution is coming down the pipeline. Whether you remain employed or not, Venus will likely find ways to keep you afloat, whether through unemployment benefits, a benefactor, or more resources to help you do your job.

Not to be overlooked is Mercury’s direct station in your 9th house of travel and learning on November 13. If you’re in school, you could get an answer about a student loan application that will possibly determine what the rest of your educational path looks like. You could also get a green light to take a trip somewhere or study abroad. It’s an interesting and eye-opening time to actually be on the road, but November’s astrology seems to be setting you up for future adventures of various kinds, so pay attention to what’s being determined and decided in these moments.

#6289. American Airlines Pilots Told Not To Eat The Tiramisu, Now Union Says Never Mind

UPDATE: The Allied Pilots Association has withdrawn its warning about tiramisu served in American Airlines crew meals in Phoenix. Following an investigation involving American’s safety team, Phoenix inflight staff, and the caterer, the union now says it was a false alarm.

Yesterday, APA ​Aeromedical was advised by the ​PHX ​Flight ​Office that ​a dessert ​included ​with ​some crew meals may ​have contained ​alcohol.

Out of ​an abundance of ​caution, APA issued an immediate ​advisory recommending that crewmembers ​not ​consume the dessert, ​specifically ​the ​tiramisu, ​until ​additional information ​could be obtained. ​Following coordination ​with ​AA ​Corporate ​Safety, PHX Inflight, ​the catering ​provider, and ​other ​involved ​parties, APA has confirmed ​that ​the desserts ​in question ​are safe ​to ​consume ​and ​do not pose a ​risk to ​aviation safety.

We appreciate the ​PHX ​Flight ​Office ​for promptly ​raising the concern and ​working with ​both American Airlines ​and APA to investigate the potential ​issue. The ​initial ​advisory ​was ​issued ​based on the information available ​at ​the ​time ​and ​with crew ​and ​flight ​safety ​as ​the priority. ​We appreciate your patience ​while additional fact finding ​was ​conducted.

For those pilots ​involved ​in a HIMS ​program ​we ​would like to ​use ​this ​as an opportunity to ​remind you that ​consuming ​certain ​food additives ​and extracts in large quantities may pose a ​risk to ​abstinence ​monitoring. Please consult ​the APA ​HIMS Subcommittee ​for additional ​information.

As ​always, ​please reach out to APA ​Aeromedical ​with any ​questions or ​concerns.

APA explained that its initial warning was precautionary, based on information available at the time…though I’m wondering what information

American Airlines pilots have been warned to skip the tiramisu in some crew meals out of Phoenix because it contains alcohol. That is an awkward ingredient to find in a meal provided to people who are supposed to be flying airplanes…

JonNYC shared a warning attributed to the Allied Pilots Association’s Aeromedical–HIMS Committee concerning meals supplied by American’s contracted caterer in Phoenix:

“The contracted catering provider has included tiramisu containing alcohol on some crew meal trays. Because the dessert is not cooked after the alcohol is added, alcohol may remain in the finished product.

“We recommend that no crew member consume this dessert.

“APA cannot determine the amount of alcohol contained in an individual serving or what effect consumption could have if a crewmember were subsequently required to undergo DOT alcohol testing.”

"PHX Crew Meal Alert – Tiramisu Containing Alcohol

The APA Aeromedical–HIMS Committee has been made aware of an issue affecting crews based in or transiting PHX.

The contracted catering provider has included tiramisu containing alcohol on some crew meal trays.…

The notice says the committee is coordinating with the Phoenix Flight Office to have the dessert removed and replaced. In the meantime, crews are advised to accept an incomplete meal rather than eat it.

Pilots who have already consumed the tiramisu and have concerns about their fitness to fly are instructed to contact their union domicile representatives immediately. The warning expressly tells them not to let schedule pressure influence that decision.

The notice does not establish that a serving would cause impairment or a failed alcohol test. The committee says it does not know the alcohol content or the potential testing consequences. But crews should not have to evaluate that uncertainty while eating an airline-provided meal!

The FAA explains that a confirmed alcohol concentration of 0.02 to 0.039 requires temporary removal from safety-sensitive duties, even though that result is not itself a federal testing violation. A confirmed result of 0.04 or greater carries more serious consequences.

American’s Phoenix caterer apparently supplied an alcohol-containing dessert in crew meals, prompting a union warning to leave it untouched while a replacement is arranged. I like tiramisu, but this is one setting where the alcohol-free version is the obvious choice. Pilots have enough to think about without wondering whether their crew meal could complicate an alcohol test…

#6288. United CEO Hints at Potential Destinations

United is exploring potential new markets in a part of the world not served by any of its U.S. competitors.

CEO Scott Kirby told the hosts of the Cheeky Pint podcast that global network planning chief Patrick Quayle and his team were recently in Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan.

“We can’t fly there today because we can’t fly over Russia,” he said. “But he’s there. This could work down the road.”

Kirby did not elaborate on plans for the region but cited United’s seasonal service to Nuuk, Greenland, as evidence that unconventional destinations can work.

No U.S. airlines currently fly to Central Asia. Russia’s ban on Western airlines – enacted in the early days of the Russia-Ukraine war – would make the trip uneconomically long.

Historically, there was little demand among American travelers for connections to Central Asia, but that is changing. American arrivals in Uzbekistan, for instance, increased from around 17,000 in 2019 to more than 26,000 in the first seven months of 2026 alone. The newfound interest has been attributed to visa liberalization measures in Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, and Kyrgyzstan, the relative affordability of the region, and trips by travel influencers.

In Kazakhstan, international airlines mainly serve Almaty, the country’s most populous city. In Uzbekistan, the main international gateway is Tashkent.

The only Central Asian carrier with flights to the U.S. is Uzbekistan Airways. The airline serves New York-JFK from Tashkent.

#6287. TAP Air Portugal Launches New U.S. Route

TAP Air Portugal on Thursday began nonstop service between Lisbon and Orlando, Florida.

The transatlantic connection will operate three times weekly, on Mondays, Thursdays, and Saturdays, using Airbus A330 aircraft. Each flight has 34 Business Class seats, 12 Economy Prime seats, and 240 Economy Class seats.

“With the launch of the route between Lisbon and Orlando, TAP Air Portugal continues to invest in strengthening its network in North America, a market of enormous importance to the airline,” Renato Inácio, TAP’s chief financial officer, said in a news release. “This new route brings Portugal closer to one of the United States’ leading tourist and economic regions, whilst offering our customers opportunities for connections throughout Europe, Africa, and South America.”

Orlando is TAP’s second destination in Florida, behind Miami, and its ninth in the U.S. Its other U.S. destinations are New York-JFK, Newark, New Jersey, Boston, Washington Dulles, Chicago O’Hare, Los Angeles, and San Francisco.

#6286. 11 Taos Airbnbs That Embody the Soul of the Southwest

From the first time my parents’ car crested the last hill on New Mexico State Road 68 en route to Taos, and the depths of the Rio Grande Gorge emerged in view, I was hooked. As a New Mexican, I’ve spent more than 30 years visiting the northern New Mexico town of Taos, where I enjoy dining on local cuisine, browsing contemporary art galleries, hiking the peaks around Taos Ski Valley, and rafting the Rio Grande rapids. As time has passed, the town’s unique charm has remained, but its popularity has only grown.

Indigenous peoples have inhabited the lands here since time immemorial, and today, the residents of Taos Pueblo welcome visitors to a stacked-adobe village whose architecture is synonymous with the Southwest. Creatives have long felt called to this area, from the likes of Ansel Adams, who turned his lens on the wide buttresses of St. Francisco de Assisi Mission Church, to Georgia O’Keeffe, who first visited in 1929.

One of the best ways to take in the local culture and enjoy the architecture is by staying in a Taos Airbnb. In this way, travelers get the chance to embrace elements of the town’s character, from its regional design to its counter-culture scene captured in the sustainable Earthships dotting the vast sagebrush mesa beneath mountain peaks. Whether you’re following your creative muse, want to embrace the desert landscape, or are eager to get a taste of Southwestern living, these are the best Taos Airbnbs to visit right now.

We've selected these listings based on Superhost and Guest Favorite status, ratings, amenities, location, decor, editor stays, and previous guest reviews.

Forget Delta One. Saturday Night Live has imagined another cabin for Delta Air Lines it calls “Delta Disruptive Class,” and this one addresses a problem even a lie-flat seat cannot solve: the passenger who makes everyone else’s flight miserable.

In a spoof commercial from its October 31 episode, Saturday Night Live introduces “Delta Disruptive,” a separate section for passengers whose behavior makes them particularly unwelcome elsewhere on the aircraft.

The premise is simple: instead of letting these travelers ruin the flight for everyone, put them together behind a thick plexiglass partition.

— Saturday Night Live (@nbcsnl), November 1, 2026

The fictional cabin accommodates everything from obnoxious personal habits to full-blown onboard meltdowns. “All Delta Disruptive flight attendants are the toughest, gayest, ex-Spirit Airlines employees who have seen much worse.”

As usual with SNL skits, the joke captures a frustrating truth about flying: as carefully as you may choose your airline seat, you cannot choose the person sitting nearby. One passenger can make an otherwise pleasant flight unbearable.

#6284. AirBaltic Moves to Cut Around 300 Employees

Distressed Latvian flag carrier airBaltic plans to lay off around 300 employees as it continues restructuring, according to the Latvian Aviation Union.

The union, which represents pilots, cabin crew, aircraft technicians, office staff, and other workers in Latvia’s airline sector, said airBaltic expects to cut around 100 pilots and 200 flight attendants. The LAU strongly opposes the move and said it has not received the carrier’s assessment criteria for which workers will be let go.

“These are people’s careers, livelihoods, and futures,” the union said. “Decisions affecting hundreds of aviation professionals must not be made through a process that lacks transparency and agreed rules.”

The LAU also called on the Latvian government to intervene in the process.

AirBaltic filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the U.S. in September. It is facing serious financial headwinds from higher jet fuel prices and route disruptions caused by conflicts in Eastern Europe and the Middle East.

The carrier is continuing to operate its normal schedule while its bankruptcy case proceeds. It mainly serves destinations in Europe but also flies to North Africa, the Middle East, Turkey, and the Caucasus.

AirBaltic has secured a commitment for €350 million, or about $403.6 million, in debtor-in possession financing, which it said will be enough to support operations during the bankruptcy process.

As we get closer to Thanksgiving, early Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales are starting to crop up, along with hot-off-the-press cruise offers and loads of airfare bargains worth keeping on your radar, including both international and domestic routes.

Are airlines using your personal data to decide what price you see when you go to book a flight?

It’s a question that has come up repeatedly over the last couple of years, and it’s back in the headlines this week.

On Wednesday, the Federal Trade Commission announced an inquiry into whether nine large companies — including three major airlines — have engaged in so-called “personalized pricing.”

That’s a tactic in which a company sets one price for you and a different price for someone else, based on information it has about you.

Imagine that you see a $300 flight from Chicago to Miami, while your friend down the street sees the same flight for $220.

The inquiry centers on three of the largest U.S. carriers: Delta Air Lines, United Airlines and JetBlue, along with major companies from several other industries.

Airlines flatly deny they use surveillance-like tactics to set fares.

“They do not engage in personalized pricing,” Airlines for America, a trade group for the largest U.S. carriers, said definitively in a statement Friday. “Our carriers rely on marketplace conditions and consumer demand for pricing, as they always have.”

Questions about airlines' ticket-pricing tactics have seemingly grown louder over the past year, though.

Last year, Delta faced scrutiny from lawmakers after executives revealed the carrier had begun using a third-party AI tool to help set flight prices.

That revelation drew backlash from Capitol Hill, though Delta insisted it was not using customers’ private information to influence fares — and never planned to.

Just this week, Thrifty Traveler’s latest investigation revealed some U.S. carriers continue to charge solo travelers higher prices than flyers booking with one companion or more.

The airline later deleted the post and said the customer service agent who wrote the comment was mistaken.

But the saga ignited a firestorm on social media that laid bare consumers’ growing concerns over how big companies might be using the information they have to set prices.

Airlines certainly do know a lot about their customers.

After all, security requirements dictate that we hand over key personal details every time we book a flight. Plus, most of us voluntarily provide airlines with even more of our information by participating in loyalty programs.

And then there's dynamic pricing, which can cause fares to change from one moment to the next as seats fill up and demand shifts — often leaving customers puzzled.

“I think people are sort of scared that the reason why they see those prices change like that is because of their behavior — them kind of searching, coming back,” Garrett Scott, a University of Mississippi economist who studies airline pricing, told me earlier this year.

“As consumers, it’s really easy to be like, 'These people are screwing us over,'" he said. “I am not 100% convinced that that is what’s going on."

Airlines are up front about some strategies they use to show different prices — specifically, award prices — to different customers.

For instance, Delta and United both offer their credit card holders automatic award discounts — a well-advertised perk of carrying certain cards.

Also, if you’ve booked a flight recently, go back and check the reservation: There’s a good chance your airline might be offering you a targeted upgrade price.

Many of these tactics, Scott argues, are entirely benign. In some cases, he notes, they can save consumers money by offering lower fares or targeted discounts when demand for a flight drops.

It appears the feds may feel the same way.

Speaking to TPG on Friday, an FTC official said the agency is less concerned about companies using personalized pricing and more concerned about them doing so without disclosing it to consumers.

To reiterate, airlines say they don't do that and don't plan to.

However, some experts argue that the lines between ordinary airline pricing tactics and surveillance pricing have begun to blur.

For instance, a carrier could decide to hike holiday fares during a week when its data shows wealthier travelers tend to book their end-of-year trips, Mark Tremblay, an expert in pricing strategies at the University of Nevada, Las Vegas, offered.

“I would argue that this is personalized pricing in disguise. But they would call it 'dynamic pricing,'” Tremblay said. “You could make a lot of arguments like this for other industries.”

And it’s not just airlines that are now under the FTC’s microscope.

The agency’s inquiry also extends to ride-hailing companies Uber and Lyft, as well as big-box retailers like Walmart and Target, and delivery service giants DoorDash and Instacart.

As part of the probe, the feds ordered those companies to turn over information on their pricing tactics — including whether fares can fluctuate based on personal factors, including participation in a loyalty program.

#6281. What Happens If Your Passport Expires While You're Abroad?

Most countries don't allow international travelers to enter their territory unless they have at least six months left before their passport expires. That might sound like an unnecessary ask for a week-long vacation, but the rule is in place for good reason.

That's because if you do find yourself in a scenario when your passport expires while you're abroad—say due to an unexpected medical issue or trip delay, for example—you could be facing a major bureaucratic headache.

However, although it might feel like a crisis, having your passport lapse while traveling is not the end of the world. There are procedures that travelers can follow to obtain a renewed document and get their trip back on track. Here’s a look at what happens if your passport expires while you’re abroad.

Many countries do not allow international tourists to visit unless they have a certain amount of validity left on their passport. A common rule of thumb that many nations observe is the six month rule: there must be at least six months before your passport expires in order to enter the country.

In some countries, including many popular destinations in the EU, your passport is required to be valid for an additional three months after your intended departure date. Before you board an international flight, airlines will verify your passport expiration and usually will not let you board the plane if your passport doesn’t meet the validity requirements. It's important to note that some airlines and cruise lines might have their own passport validity policies that differ from the country's official requirements, so be sure to check both.

Sometimes, it’s possible to enter a different country and stay past your passport’s expiration date. If that's the case, the protocol you’ll need to follow is similar to when a passport is lost or stolen abroad.

First, you’ll need to contact the nearest US embassy or consulate for assistance. If you’re not sure where the nearest embassy or consulate might be, you can use the search tool on the State Department’s website. You’ll need to then visit the embassy or consulate location in person in order to have them issue you a new passport. Keep in mind this could mean you need to travel to a different city within the country you’re visiting.

When you arrive, you’ll essentially need to apply for a new passport. That means you’ll need to bring:

“Even if you cannot present all these documents, consular staff will do their best to help you get a new passport quickly,” the State Department’s site says.

US citizens abroad who have urgent travel plans are usually issued an emergency passport, which is valid for up to one year. However, it’s also possible to get a full-validity passport that doesn’t expire for 10 years. It will depend on the specifics of your situation.

Replacement passports are usually issued by the next business day, according to the State Department.

If you’re a US citizen living overseas for an extended period of time, you might qualify for routine passport renewal by mail through the nearest US embassy or consulate. Processing times for renewal by mail are usually about four to six weeks, not including shipping time. Visit the website of the local embassy or consulate in your area and follow their instructions for passport renewal.
